catalog_quote: The present writer has information from his own fieldnotes, on the structures of Nambu and Iauga (Parb) which are virtually identical. The following notes reflect only their features. The phonology is quite complex, and the following statements are also tentative. ... Vowel length is phonemic. Several diphthongs are found. The suprasegmental system appears to consist of a relatively complex stress system with rhythm principles, but no tonal system seems to be present. The syllable structure is of some complexity.

new_statements.rule_in_words: No rule given. Wurm only says that the 'Nambu' language (his 1971 cover term for the varieties of Mibini, Garaita, Setavi, Mata, Saraina, Pongaki, Gubam, Keru, Derideri, Arufi and Tais — Keru being the Neme village) has a 'relatively complex stress system with rhythm principles' and no tone; the sentence is tentative, based on unspecified fieldnotes, and is the same formula he uses for most Trans-Fly families. Stress position is not stated. No source states where word stress falls in Neme.
new_statements.domain_note: Group-level statement about 'Nambu' as a single language, not about the Keru/Neme variety specifically; almost certainly based on a Nambo/Nama-area variety. Sister languages described since: Nen initial stress with morphological/weight conditions (Evans & Miller 2016), Nmbo obligatory stress tending to the penult (Kashima 2020: 109), Nama stress described in Siegel 2023 §2.4.3 (paywalled). Kashima 2020: 49 states that descriptions of Neme remain to be conducted.
new_statements.identity_note: Neme = the language of Keru and Mitere villages (Rueck 2011: 67, 113); Kashima 2020 calls it Keru. Glottolog/Wikipedia give the alternative names Dorro, Karigari, Moi-e/Moive, but Wurm 1971: 152 locates 'Dorro' in Mari village, which Rueck 2011 assigns to Namo (Mari, Tais), so the old 'Dorro' wordlists (Riley & Ray 1930-31) may belong to Namo rather than Neme. Wurm's stress sentence is about his aggregate 'Nambu' language, whose village list includes Keru; it is not a description of the Keru/Neme variety and does not give a position. Not to be confused with Aneme Wake ('Neme', Oro Province) or Nema.
